title: Reduce and find, with the right identity and an honest Optional

blocks.text: `reduce` folds a stream into one value. With an identity, `reduce(identity, op)` returns a plain value, and the identity is what an empty stream gives back, so it must leave every element unchanged (`0` for `+`, `1` for `*`). Without one, `reduce(op)` returns an `Optional`, which is empty for an empty stream. `findFirst()` returns an `Optional` too.

items: `int product(List<Integer> numbers)`: the product of all the numbers.
`String firstStartingWith(List<String> words, String prefix, String fallback)`: the first word, in list order, that starts with `prefix`, or `fallback` when none does.

blocks.text: "Starts with" means `String.startsWith`: the prefix is plain text, matched case-sensitively at the start of the word. Think about what each method owes an empty list, a list of negative numbers, and a prefix nothing starts with.

cases.says: It multiplies the numbers and finds the largest one.
It returns the first word, in list order, that starts with the prefix.
The product of an empty list is 1, the identity of multiplication, not 0.
The largest of all-negative numbers is negative: 0 is no identity for max.
An empty list has no largest number, so the result is an empty Optional, not a sentinel.
When no word matches, the fallback comes back instead of a NoSuchElementException.
"crab" and "Bay" do not start with "b", and "bax" does not start with "b.": the prefix is plain text, case-sensitive, at the start.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: The Optional from findFirst, min, max or reduce is handled with orElse, never with a bare get().
The identity of reduce must leave every element unchanged, and it is what an empty stream returns.
Without an identity, reduce returns an Optional that is empty for an empty stream.
